articles.title: Building Satark: How I used Gemini AI to Protect India from Digital Fraud
articles.excerpt: India's digital payment ecosystem is booming. From UPI transactions at a roadside tea stall to online banking, the convenience is unparalleled. But with this rapid digitization comes a dark side: a ma…
articles.body: India's digital payment ecosystem is booming. From UPI transactions at a roadside tea stall to online banking, the convenience is unparalleled. But with this rapid digitization comes a dark side: a massive surge in cyber extortion, digital arrest scams, and phishing attacks. As a 17-year-old engineering student pursuing my BE in CSE with a specialization in AI & ML at Sapthagiri NPS University, I realized that my parents and grandparents were extremely vulnerable to these sophisticated attacks. I wanted to build something that didn't just flash a generic "Warning" sign, but actually explained the threat in simple terms and told them exactly what to do next.
articles.author: SANJAY U BHARADWAJ

articles.title: Building AI-Powered Self-Healing Deployment Systems
articles.excerpt: I got tired of the same deployment story: the deploy "succeeds", the health checks go green, and then something weird happens an hour later and the on-call person is pulling logs at 2 AM trying to fig…
articles.body: I got tired of the same deployment story: the deploy "succeeds", the health checks go green, and then something weird happens an hour later and the on-call person is pulling logs at 2 AM trying to figure out what changed. This pattern pushed me toward exploring AI-powered self-healing deployment systems — not just verifying that the deploy worked, but ensuring the service is actually behaving correctly after the deploy. Why Traditional Approaches Fall Short Health checks are necessary but insufficient. They tell you if a service is responding, not if it's functioning correctly. Traditional monitoring alerts you when things break, but doesn't help prevent issues or intelligently remediate them.
articles.author: Vectoral AI

articles.title: ParkerLabel: CPU-only image annotation with MobileSAM
articles.excerpt: I open-sourced ParkerLabel, a desktop tool for object detection and instance segmentation annotation. It runs locally on the CPU. No GPU or image upload is needed. In AI mode, positive and negative cl…
articles.body: I open-sourced ParkerLabel, a desktop tool for object detection and instance segmentation annotation. It runs locally on the CPU. No GPU or image upload is needed. In AI mode, positive and negative clicks guide MobileSAM to generate an object mask. You can correct it manually, assign a category, and save the annotation. The interface has separate image, mask, and overlay views. The inference path uses ONNX Runtime. The image embedding is saved beside the image and reused. Each instance keeps its own mask, category, bounding box, and area in a per-image JSON file. Masks use uncompressed COCO RLE; these files are not a complete COCO dataset export. There are portable packages for macOS arm64 and Windows x64.

articles.title: Recruiters search booleans, not keywords
articles.excerpt: Recruiters search with logic, not with lists of buzz‑words. When a hiring team opens a profile, they often run a query like python OR (django AND rest). The shape of that query is what determines whet…
articles.body: Recruiters search with logic, not with lists of buzz‑words. When a hiring team opens a profile, they often run a query like python OR (django AND rest). The shape of that query is what determines whether your experience lands in the first‑round candidates or gets filtered out before a human sees it. The Boolean Lens of Talent Acquisition Recruiters and hiring managers build a mental filter around the roles they need to fill. To keep the pipeline lean, they encode that filter as a boolean statement. It looks simple on the surface, but it captures intent in a way that a plain keyword list cannot. OR expands the net: python OR django will pull anyone with either skill. AND tightens the net: (django AND rest) requires both to be present. Parentheses group criteria so the logic is preserved.

articles.title: Best In-Browser Video Compressor: We Tested 4 That Never Upload Your Video
articles.excerpt: Originally published on the RedPanda Compress blog. A growing number of video compressors promise that your file never leaves your computer. Instead of uploading the video to a server, they compress i…
articles.body: Originally published on the RedPanda Compress blog . A growing number of video compressors promise that your file never leaves your computer. Instead of uploading the video to a server, they compress it inside the browser tab. That's good for privacy and it means no upload wait, but "runs in your browser" covers some very different technology. We ran the same video through the four in-browser compressors that actually get search traffic and measured what came back. Disclosure: I build RedPanda Compress, which is one of the four tools tested. It went through the same procedure as everyone else, and I report where it lost. The short answer Best quality for a given file size: RedPanda Compress. It hit our 50 MB target exactly with a VMAF score of 84.0.

articles.title: manygit: An AI-powered Git management CLI for many Git repos at once
articles.excerpt: I keep fourteen Git repositories in one folder. A few services, shared packages, plugins. Most of my work at Blend-ed touches more than one of them, so a normal question like “did I push that fix?” tu…
articles.body: I keep fourteen Git repositories in one folder. A few services, shared packages, plugins. Most of my work at Blend-ed touches more than one of them, so a normal question like “did I push that fix?” turns into a small tour of my filesystem. Open a repo. Check the branch. Run git status . Move to the next one. Forget what the first one said. I wrote about that problem in my first manygit post . The tool started as a way to put every repo’s state on one screen. Since then, I’ve added a way to ask for Git operations in plain English, across that same tree of repositories. That’s the AI part of manygit. You describe the work, read the commands it proposes, and decide whether to run them.
